verdict.line: You lose if you let him stack Q and land W (Path Maker) stuns before level 6; you win if you survive to Rylai's Crystal Scepter and force extended fights.

brief.thesis: K'Sante holds lane and solo-kill advantage through his Q (Ntofo Strikes) poke-into-shockwave and his level 3-6 all-in window with W (Path Maker) and R (All Out), but Mordekaiser's 51% head-to-head win rate over 1,848 games shows the lane flips once his core items land. This is a matchup you survive early and win late, not one you contest for kills before 6.

theirWindow.when: He hits 2 Q (Ntofo Strikes) stacks on you
theirWindow.what: At 2 stacks his Q fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in — back out of his Q range before the second hit lands, or expect to be yanked into a follow-up auto and possible W (Path Maker) stun.

yourWindow.what: Footwork is his only non-Flash mobility/shield tool, on a 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s cooldown. Once it's down he has no reset — walk him down with Q (Obliterate) and threaten E (Death's Grasp) to pull him into a full trade.

start.item: Doran's Ring + Health Potion + Health Potion
start.why: Taken in 78% of games (51.7% win rate, 1,711 games) — the extra sustain offsets his Q poke and funds Q/E mana costs through the early trade window where he holds the advantage.

boots.why: Picked in 69.1% of games at 52.2% win rate — flattens the repeated physical hits from his Q (Ntofo Strikes) and auto-reset harass that defines his early trading pattern.

core.why: Highest-win-rate path (63.9% over 119 games) — the slow on Q/E lets you stick to him through his Footwork dashes instead of losing him mid-trade.
Converts your W (Indestructible) stored damage into sustained fight-winning power once you're forced into extended skirmishes post-6.
Scales your Q/E damage against his tank stats, which is where the matchup flips in your favor after level 11.

runes.keystoneWhy: Taken in 42.6% of games (50.8% win rate) — Conqueror ramps during the exact prolonged skirmishes your E (Death's Grasp) pulls create, and the healing conversion pairs with your W (Indestructible) shield to win extended trades rather than burst ones.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is both the most picked (69.5%) and highest-win-rate (52.6%) combo in this matchup — Ignite punishes his Footwork heal when he tries to sustain through poke. Flash+Teleport (47.1%, 22.9% pick) is the alternative if you're playing fully for the scaling advantage and want to reset waves instead of threatening early skirmishes.

playing.title: Don't fight into stacked Q
playing.detail: Track his Ntofo Strikes stack count — at 2 stacks his Q fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in. Disengage before the second hit lands instead of eating the pull into a follow-up combo.

playing.title: Hold W for his all-in
playing.detail: Indestructible stores damage dealt and taken into a shield you consume for healing. Don't pop it on his Q chip damage — save the stored shield for when he commits his W (Path Maker) stun or R (All Out).

playing.title: Punish Footwork cooldown
playing.detail: His E (Footwork) dash+shield is his only non-Flash reset, on a 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s cooldown. Once it's down, walk him down with Q (Obliterate) — he has no way to disengage or re-shield.

playing.title: Respect level 3-5 W timing
playing.detail: Once he hits W (Path Maker) at level 3+, letting him charge uninterrupted risks a stun-and-knockback combo. Stay at max E (Death's Grasp) range or force the charge before you commit to a Q trade.

playing.title: Time your passive proc
playing.detail: Darkness Rise triggers an aura and move speed after 3 landed attacks or spells on champions. Sequence your Q/auto rotation so the proc lands when he's forced to stand and trade, not while he's kiting on Footwork.

playing.title: Scale through Rylai's before forcing
playing.detail: Lane and solo-kill advantage sit with him through mid-game. Play for CS and level parity until Rylai's Crystal Scepter completes — that's the item that flips extended Q/E trades in your favor.

playing.title: Save R for isolated picks
playing.detail: Realm of Death drags him away from his team and steals his stats permanently if you kill him. Use it post-6 on a solo overextension or when his own R (All Out) leaves him isolated near you — not as a poke tool.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, win rates, and sample sizes above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the tactical reading — power windows, trade patterns, and tells — is my own analysis layered on top of that data.
